long_biography.plain_text:
In 1980, Enrique Tomeu took over Siboney Contracting, the South Florida trucking company founded by his father. He broadened its material mix, bought quarry and fill operations, and added asphalt paving and site development. Selling its trucks became a strategic pivot: Siboney reorganised around an independent-carrier network and a specialist logistics team instead of an owned fleet.

The model carried the business beyond Florida, pairing bulk-material sourcing with road and barge transport for construction, agriculture, energy and disaster recovery. Tomeu also became president of Palm Beach Aggregates and invested in its rock-mining and land interests. He remains Siboney's owner and chief executive and serves on the Economic Council of Palm Beach County's board.
